stem:
Aarav sorts objects beyond the Solar System: the Milky Way Galaxy, other galaxies, and exoplanets around other stars. Whether life exists elsewhere is still unknown.

Which claim organises these ideas correctly?

options.text: The Milky Way is our galaxy; other galaxies lie beyond it; exoplanets orbit other stars; life elsewhere is not yet known.
A planet revolving around another star in the Milky Way is itself a galaxy.
The Milky Way Galaxy sits inside the Solar System.
Finding exoplanets proves that living things exist on those planets.

teacher.key_rationale: Beyond the Solar System: our Milky Way, then other galaxies; exoplanets orbit other stars; life elsewhere remains unknown. Calling an exoplanet a galaxy, placing the Milky Way inside the Solar System, or treating exoplanets as proof of life miss that hinge.
